note: Colorado River District campground and marina on Wolford Mountain Reservoir, 10 mi north of Kremmling on US-40. Four loops on a point in the reservoir: A-C electric, D non-electric; sites are not level, so bring levelers. Winter camping in Loop A only. Boat ramp, marina, swim beach. --Claude
summary: Operator site + Firefly engine + Colorado River District page: confirmed $35-40 (2026; engine $40 for a Class C), 75 sites, electric 50 with central water/dump, year-round (winter FCFS, Loop A only), reservable with some first-come; added max length 50 (engine), weekend 2-night / holiday 3-night minimums, booking.season 05-01..11-30, Firefly booking URL; cleared pull_through (not stated). Note rewritten. Ownership should be local (see flags).
flags: OWNERSHIP private -> local: the Colorado River District (Colorado River Water Conservation District, a public special district) owns the reservoir and recreation area and runs the campground's winter season ('Please make checks out to the Colorado River District'; winter camping contact kdavidson@crwcd.org); special events need 'approved in writing by the River District'. The summer operation 'Wolford Campground & Marina' is presumably a District contractor - no concessionaire is named anywhere.
Phone: stored 970-724-1266 is only the Group Camp Area C line on the operator's page; the operator's main number everywhere (home, contact, footer) is 970-531-8466. Suggest 970-531-8466.

US$50 gate: $40 for an electric site (engine quote $40.00 for a 23-ft Class C on Oct 29 2026; reservations for 2027 not yet open, posted 2026 rate $40). Passes. Nearest gateway Rocky Mountain NP 51 km; the family has not stayed here.
Presence: operator website with phone and a working Firefly engine. Passes. Not long-stay in character (nightly sites sold online; the monthly price is only for group areas).
Engine rig types: Firefly asks for equipment type and offers Motorhome Class A/B/C; quoted as Class C 23 ft. No van-only class.

Waterfront (stored lakeview): consistent, possible upgrade lead. The four loops sit on a point with the reservoir on three sides; the outer sites of the two east loops are roughly 50-100 m from the high-water line across open sage and a drawdown beach, with nothing blocking the view. Whether that meets the open-apron rule for lakefront is for a re-audit.

Status: home-page notice 9/19/26 'Boat Ramp has been closed; Water fill and dump station will be winterized Wednesday, September 30th' - ordinary seasonal shutdown; campground open year-round. Not a status.
Site layout: the old note's '40-43 ft rigs, some pull-throughs' had no current source; the engine gives 32-50 ft per site and no drive-through type, so pull_through was cleared rather than kept.
